explanation: This test only verifies that the FX rate shown matches the rate at initiation, which partially covers the 'fx_lock' requirement. It does not test the transactional sequence of crediting the destination wallet before debiting the funding source ('credit_before_debit'), nor does it test the dual approval requirement for top-ups above SGD 10,000 ('dual_approval'). The test also lacks any verification of the actual wallet balances or the rollback behavior on payment provider timeout. It misses asserting that the funding source is debited only after the destination wallet is credited, and it does not check for the approval workflow for large top-ups.
missingAssertions: Assert that the destination wallet balance increases before the funding source balance decreases
Assert that top-ups above SGD 10,000 require second-owner approval before settlement
hypothesizedBugThisWouldMiss: A bug where the funding source is debited before the destination wallet is credited would not be caught, as the test does not verify the order of these operations. Also, a bug where top-ups above SGD 10,000 proceed without second-owner approval would be missed.

suggestedReplacement.description: Verify transactional integrity of multi-currency wallet top-up including FX rate lock, credit-before-debit sequence, and dual approval for large amounts
steps: Initiate top-up of USD 100 and record FX rate at initiation
Verify that the FX rate used matches the recorded rate
Verify that the destination wallet balance increases immediately after initiation
Verify that the funding source is debited only after the destination wallet is credited
Verify that the system requests second-owner approval before settlement
Simulate payment provider callback timeout after 5 seconds
Verify that the transaction is rolled back and neither wallet nor funding source balances change
suggestedReplacement.expectedResult: FX rate is locked at initiation; destination wallet is credited before funding source is debited; top-ups above SGD 10,000 require second-owner approval before settlement; transaction rolls back if payment provider callback times out
